title: Depression to Dictatorship Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace how economic collapse turned the Nazis from a fringe group into Germany's dictatorship.
meta_desc: GCSE History — how the Depression and political deals brought Hitler to power 1929-1934.
final_note: You learned how the Depression boosted the Nazis, Hitler became Chancellor, and the Enabling Act crushed democracy.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1928 the Nazis won just 2.6% of votes.

The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 changed everything. Unemployment in Germany rose to around 6 million by 1932. Voters abandoned moderate parties.

In July 1932 the Nazis became the biggest party in the Reichstag with 230 seats.

President Hindenburg refused to make Hitler Chancellor at first. But after political deals with von Papen, Hitler was appointed Chancellor on 30 January 1933.

The Reichstag Fire on 27 February 1933 let Hitler suppress Communists.

The Enabling Act of March 1933 gave him the power to make laws without the Reichstag. After Hindenburg died in August 1934, Hitler became Führer.
